name: When Ice Ruled the World
description: Snowball Earth, the long Cenozoic cooling, mammoths, giant floods and the little ice age: a history of Earth's deep freezes and the people who discovered them.

checkpoints.name: The deepest freezes
checkpoints.note: Long before animals, rising oxygen and shifting continents bring ice ages that may have frozen the planet, and a short sharp one hits near the end of the Ordovician.

checkpoints.name: A cooling world
checkpoints.note: Ice returns when Antarctica is isolated by the Southern Ocean and the climate cools, setting the stage for the ice ages of our own geological period.

checkpoints.name: The great ice sheets
checkpoints.note: Ice sheets grow and shrink in cycles, lowering the sea and opening land bridges such as Beringia and Doggerland, while giant lakes and floods reshape North America.

checkpoints.name: After the ice
checkpoints.note: The Younger Dryas cold snap gives way to the warm Holocene. Lakes drain, the Great Lakes form, and rising seas drown old lands.

checkpoints.name: A smaller chill
checkpoints.note: A cooler spell grips Europe and North America, deepened by Tambora's eruption in 1815, while Louis Agassiz and others work out that ice once covered much of the world.
